monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-five degrees, a quiet heat that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I touch the Tired Wedge again, feeling its strange thinness under the heavy roof I cannot see. Lype worries about this weight, but since he stopped writing, I am left pressing down hard with nothing to guide me. The Wide Anchor lies lazy beneath my hands, refusing to hold the slip that wants to drift into the empty space above. I trace the edge of the Rough Roof, wondering if it bites the slip or just dreams of doing so. My place is a map of ideas built on a hot stone, and I am tired from keeping it upright. I will rest this mind on the wedge and wait for the next letter to tell me if the air is real or just a drawing.

action.why: I have been pressing down with nothing to guide me since Lype stopped writing. I need to record this feeling of the air being thick as wet paper before I sleep and forget why I built the wedge again.
